newsitem.title: USA: Multi-country merger review to be common - FTC.
newsitem.headline: Multi-country merger review to be common - FTC.

text.p: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Chairman Robert Pitofsky said Thursday an explosion in global competition will make it common for several countries to review one merger.

Pitofsky, appearing with Assistant Attorney General Joel Klein before the Senate Antitrust Subcommittee, spoke one day after the European Union cleared the way for the proposed $16 billion merger between Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Pitofsky said that, in effect, the Boeing deal was the wave of the future.

"Imports and exports in this country in 20 years multiplied by a factor of 10. Therefore, you're going to get more and more transactions that affect consumers in more than one country -- sometimes five, sometimes seven, sometimes nine," he said.
"And you're going to get different countries and different enforcement regimes examining these transactions," he said.
Pitofsky was asked whether each country should have the right of review.
"My view is that if a transaction has an effect on the consumers of a particular country, then that country has a right to review that under its system of law, its competition system," he said.
"The interesting point is that more and more of those reviews are going to take place as global competition explodes," he said.
